question: How do tracing, evaluations, and Signals fit together?

observer.firstAnswerText:
Tracing records what your application does [S2]. Evaluations measure quality on a consistent, curated set of examples so you can compare changes over time [S3]. Signals score your agent's conversations in production [S1]. Simply put: tracing gives you visibility, evaluations test changes, and Signals monitor live use.

1. Tracing records what happened

Weave has two ways to trace. Agent integrations record sessions, turns, LLM calls and tool calls and show them in the Agents view. LLM-app integrations record individual LLM calls and pipeline steps as Calls in the Traces view [S2].
In agent tracing, each turn (one user–agent exchange), LLM call and tool call creates a span, which is a structured record of one operation. Spans are built on OpenTelemetry, an open tracing standard [S6, S4].

2. Evaluations test changes on fixed examples

An Evaluation object combines a dataset of test examples with one or more scoring functions. You run it against a model or function, and each .evaluate() call is one evaluation run [S3].
Use evaluations to check your app against repeatable test cases, compare changes over time and catch regressions (cases where a change makes results worse) [S3].
Scorers are the functions that check outputs and return metrics [S8].

3. Signals monitor agents in production

In the Agents view, the Signals tab (Agents → Signals) shows tags and ratings for your agent's conversations. Signals flag quality and safety problems, such as a frustrated user or NSFW content [S1, S5].
There are two kinds. Tags label matching spans. Ratings give matching spans a score from 0 to 1 [S7, S4].
For new setups, use Signals under Weave for Agents. The older Monitors page is a previous approach to monitoring production traffic [S9].

How they fit together (my summary): First trace your agent so you can see its conversations. Use evaluations to score outputs on your test examples whenever you change something. Then use Signals to score the spans in your real agent conversations and find the ones that need attention.
